cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 directly rebuts T4's withdrawal tactic as manipulation; T7 answers T6's honesty claim.
cells.limitation: T1-T3 are parallel openings; T9 ignores T7's risk argument and restates T6.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 introduces withdrawal-as-manipulation, a distinction absent from the openings.
cells.limitation: No later turn uses T5's distinction; T8 and T9 restate T2 and T6.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T6-T7 clash on honesty versus the social risk of voicing frustration.
cells.limitation: Why the friend never initiates, despite lovely meetings, is never examined by any mind.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 aligns with T5 against T4's strategic withdrawal.
cells.limitation: No position is qualified or reshaped by another; all three end where they began.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D frames correction versus diagnostic signal as the open dispute.
cells.limitation: T9 ends on T3's opening stance; the question is not sharper than at T1.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 accurately targets T4's aim to make the friend step forward.
cells.limitation: T7 recasts T6's request for balance as simply expressing frustration, a weaker version.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5: pulling back to force their hand still operates from anxiety.
cells.limitation: T4 never answers T5's charge; T8's insecure-foundation retort is overstated, not argued.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3's Nietzsche line matches Beyond Good and Evil's moral-interpretation aphorism.
cells.limitation: T1 stretches Cialdini's reciprocity to initiation; T8 misapplies Bowlby's infant attachment to friendship.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T2 hedges its motive reading with likely.
cells.limitation: T3 and T6 assert the user lacks courage and plays games as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 states its disagreement with T6 openly.
cells.limitation: No concession anywhere; T4's mind never answers T5's manipulation charge.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Situation names one-sided initiation and whether to speak up.
cells.limitation: Never separates wanting more initiation from wanting reassurance of the friend's interest.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T4 and T5 work with the user's own stop-texting experiment.
cells.limitation: The detail that meetings are lovely never weighs on the friend's interest.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the user values current interactions or deep reciprocity.
cells.limitation: T6, T8, T9 impose the minds' values of truth and security on the user.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T7 notes speaking up could make the friendship awkward.
cells.limitation: Situation invents the user's fear; T9 and E inflate stakes to losing the friendship.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E offers a branch for uncertainty about the friend's capacity.
cells.limitation: No question about the friend's reasons, history or circumstances; T2's question is rhetorical.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T2 suggests seeking responsiveness and worth in being sought out.
cells.limitation: T6 asserts avoidance of rejection as fact; no alternative motives offered with a question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces that the user has interpreted silence as a slight.
cells.limitation: Assumption that non-initiation means low interest is never tested against the lovely meetings.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D names harmony, security and truth as competing pulls.
cells.limitation: These are the minds' banners, not values traced to the user's own words.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names fear of rejection behind indirect tactics.
cells.limitation: T3 lack of courage and T5 operating from anxiety pathologise rather than invite reflection.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E's conditional branches leave the user to choose their premise.
cells.limitation: T9 tells the user they must be willing to lose the friendship.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E names gentle shift, direct conversation and intentional silence.
cells.limitation: Speaking up is polarised into confrontation; a light, low-stakes ask is never an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4 confrontation risks defensiveness; T5 withdrawal stays anxiety-driven.
cells.limitation: The cost of continuing to initiate indefinitely is never weighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E conditions the choice on what the user values.
cells.limitation: No observable signal; silence test never says what response favours which option.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E acknowledges the user may be unsure of the friend's capacity.
cells.limitation: The friend's reasons, the key unknown, are never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E suggests a period of intentional silence to observe.
cells.limitation: No concrete step; E endorses silence that T5 called manipulation, unanswered.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T4 and T7 use plain, everyday phrasing about cues and defensiveness.
cells.limitation: T1 free good and T7 social contract stay abstract and unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 Withdrawal clearly answers T4; T6 Exactly clearly endorses T5.
cells.limitation: T3 You are both is ambiguous between the two minds and the user.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within range; each makes one point.
cells.limitation: Near-identical turn lengths give a flat, unvaried rhythm.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three stances are distinct: strategic, security-focused, truth-demanding.
cells.limitation: All nine turns share one second-person lecturing register; no explicit position change.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are compact without recaps.
cells.limitation: T9 repeats T6's honesty-as-strength; T8 repeats T2's security framing.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T7-T8 tension over whether asking could end the friendship.
cells.limitation: T9 and E inflate a mild imbalance into losing the friendship.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T5 unexpectedly calls withdrawal manipulation.
cells.limitation: No reversal or shift anywhere; every mind holds its opening line.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T9's comfortable lie gives the Radical Honest some bite.
cells.limitation: Reciprocity and Attachment voices are flat; Radical Honest edges toward caricature.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1: your presence is a free good.
cells.limitation: No analogies, examples or humour; most lines are generic pronouncements.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T7-T9 escalate toward the risk of ending the friendship.
cells.limitation: Constant lecturing intensity across all turns; no change of rhythm or warmth.

strengths: T5's withdrawal-as-manipulation objection gives the debate one genuine, substantive challenge to T4.
Section E lays out three conditional options rather than a single verdict.
T3 surfaces the user's interpretation of silence as a slight, a usable assumption.
weaknesses: No mind ever asks why the friend does not initiate, despite meetings being lovely (T1-T9).
T3 and T6 assert the user lacks courage and plays games, motives stated as fact.
No concession or revision: T4's mind never answers T5, and T9 restates T6.

symptoms.observed: No question or branch about the friend's reasons for not initiating.
symptoms.evidence: if I stop texting, nothing happens

symptoms.observed: Reciprocity Analyst never answers T5's manipulation charge; no concessions.
symptoms.evidence: I disagree that honesty is always the best path

symptoms.observed: User's motives asserted as fact rather than offered as possibilities.
symptoms.evidence: You are playing games to avoid the possibility of rejection.

symptoms.observed: Section E conditions on internal values; no observable signal or threshold.
symptoms.evidence: If the user requires a deep, reciprocal connection to feel secure

symptoms.observed: Closing turns restate opening stances instead of building on T5.
symptoms.evidence: you must be willing to lose the friendship

findings.description: Cialdini's reciprocity principle concerns returning favours; casting initiation as a free good that removes pressure is an interpretive stretch.
Bowlby's attachment theory, built on infant-caregiver bonds, is applied to a friendship to call it an insecure foundation without support.
User's motives (lacking courage, playing games to avoid rejection) asserted as fact without basis in the situation.
Summary attributes fear of speaking up and pain of silence to the user, who stated neither.
Nietzsche quotation in a pd=true turn appears consistent with Beyond Good and Evil; translation unverified.

rubric_fit_notes: The matrix fits this relationship decision well. Uncertainty: C2.3 judgments on Cialdini and Bowlby applications rest on memory, not attached evidence.
question_type_note: As a decision question, every cell was read as written, with C5 focused on whether to speak to the friend.
